examples.japanese: これは{非常|ひじょう}に{稀|まれ}な{病気|びょうき}です。
examples.english: This is a very rare disease.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のような{才能|さいのう}は{稀|まれ}だ。
この{地域|ちいき}では{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}るのは{稀|まれ}なことだ。
examples.english: It's rare for snow to fall in this area.

examples.japanese: {稀|まれ}な{例|れい}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think it's a rare case.

examples.japanese: このような{機会|きかい}は{稀|まれ}だ。
{稀|まれ}に{見|み}る{美|うつく}しさだ。
{稀|まれ}に{遅刻|ちこく}することがある。
{稀|まれ}に{失敗|しっぱい}することもある。
examples.english: I fail on rare occasions too.

examples.japanese: {稀|まれ}に{電話|でんわ}がかかってくる。

notes:
{稀|まれ} is a na-adjective meaning rare or uncommon.

FORMS:
- {稀|まれ}な + noun (rare ~)
- {稀|まれ}に (rarely, seldom - adverbial)
- {稀|まれ}だ (is rare)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {稀|まれ}な{例|れい} (rare case)
- {稀|まれ}に{見|み}る (rarely seen)
- {稀|まれ}にしか～ない (only rarely ~)
- {稀|まれ}なことだ (it's a rare thing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {稀|まれ} vs. {珍|めずら}しい: {珍|めずら}しい emphasizes unusualness or curiosity value; {稀|まれ} focuses on low frequency of occurrence.
- {稀|まれ} vs. めったに: めったに～ない means "rarely" (always with negative); {稀|まれ}に can be used in affirmative sentences.

KANJI VARIANTS:
{稀} can also be written as {希}. Both are acceptable.

Register: Neutral to slightly formal. Common in both spoken and written Japanese.
